Legally Blonde.notes: MY NOTES: FANTASTIC audio!!! The quality is amazingly clear which makes for a great performance. Jason DeBord conducted this performance and the subtle changes to the score were so nice to hear. Sounds like Laura blows a raspberry at Christian after he says "the room just got colder" in Chip, and he is trying not to laugh until the transition. Rufus also starts barking before Kyle exits following the ballad, which leads to some improv from both Matthew and Orfeh. Andy was better as Callahan compared to the first audio I listened with him, but the choices he made I still didn't really like. Great performances from everyone!

MY NOTES: Very nice audio. LOTS of applause, especially at entrances. Laura got a full minute! Cast was having a fun time, doing some random things that they normally wouldn’t. Some different line choices, but most was visual stuff and the only real way to tell is the laughter. Christian doing the bend and snap was incredible (you can hear him drop the file). I don’t think Laura’s “slip up” is that, she thanks DeQuina instead of Pilar right before What You Want. Laura was also having a time singing the ballad, and the “I found my way to love” part of the finale is just sung by Christian. Orfeh riffs most of Ireland (Reprise) and brings back the bone cake line from San Francisco. A very fun listen for fans of the show!

GENERAL NOTES: Kate Rockwell's first Elle. Had to record in STLP instead of ST because of space constraints on my dvr, due to the last-minuteness of attending. Act I audio'd from center orch- you can hear a couple of chatty aud members thru Omigod You Guys, I moved my dvr after. Kate Rockwell messed up one line in Chip, and had a delayed entrance from the Chip costume change (Christian Borle had to vamp- “I see...pink...” etc.), otherwise her Elle was brilliant.

Nikki and Nic are an excellent leading pair; Nic executes the optional high A in “Chip on My Shoulder” on “never can tell” effortlessly. Hannah sings the hell out of Legally Blonde (Remix) and it’s fun to hear an early performance from the now star. The rest of the company is also excellent; Jillian sings the end of Ireland (Reprise) slightly differently than we’ve heard before. Tracked.

Merrily We Roll Along.notes:
Clear audio recorded from the front orchestra of the first performance after the 77th Tony Awards. This was also one of the performances filmed for the pro-shot. Extremely enthusiastic audience - clapping and cheering occasionally overpowers the cast and orchestra during the opening. Overall it was a very well-behaved audience (probably due to the filming), so minimal, if any, extra noises. Audio becomes muffled during the standing ovation for It’s A Hit!, but clears right before the dialogue resumes. Recording includes curtain call and playout music for those who like to have it, but the sound is slightly muffled on and off throughout these parts.

That said, Kathy is a lovely, lovely Marian who sings the songs beautifully in the keys as written, which is such a treat. Jayne Houdyshell left no scenery unchewed. This is the kind of role Hugh Jackman is perfect for (deception? By someone who hangs with the Trumps? Never!), and he is pretty stellar, in my humble opinion.

Some Like it Hot.notes: merry late Christmas. one of the last shows before closing. my first time sitting the the mezzanine! I couldnt find where exactly it happened, but sometime within the first 5-10 minutes, I had to get up to let some people into their seats - so there might be some muffled audio/lots of talking. act 2 is only about 40 minutes long - I dont know how that happened and didnt realize until exporting and noticing it seemed way too short. Im not familiar enough with the show to know how much is missing exactly, but I assume its a decent 20ish minutes. its a good audio, even if Im a mess. J. Harrison Ghee is such a talent that they elevated what, to me, was an otherwise dull show outside of the big dance sequences. includes several split up clips of bows since my phone kept interrupting the video lmao.

Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet.notes:
First preview! Includes the “Johanna (Mea Culpa)” and a reprise for Sweeney of “Not While I'm Around” in the “Final Sequence.” Also, a fair number of other differences from the version that opened, including the fact that Mrs. Lovett is included in the opening “Ballad of Sweeney Todd,” some slightly different choral arrangements, and some slightly different vocal lines. Lansbury goes up on her lyrics during “Worst Pies in London” and “By the Sea,” and ends up singing a series of “la la las” for several bars on the latter.

There are three versions of this audio in circulation. 

AIFF (tracked) - 1.54 GB (52 files) is directly from the Master who recorded this and is the best/correct quality.
MP3 (tracked) - 143 MB (60 files) has track 221 is mislabeled as 219, though some traders have corrected this. Not a 1st gen. 
MP3 (tracked) - 358 MB (52 files) appears to be a lower gen copy, but is not the original 1st Gen.
